Variants.Content: The Portley family, based in King's Harbor near Pike, was an important sea-facing vassal of the Iron Islands. Ports, fishing grounds, longships, and distance from pike determine the weight of a family; King's Harbor not only allows sailors and merchants to gather, but also becomes a target for rebellion, conquests, and revenge at sea. The Ironborn family's reputation is often overshadowed by tales of loot and raids, but Botley must maintain a daily existence amid pirates, storms, salt taxes, and the barrenness of the island. To the people of the island, the lord's bravery only really meant something when he brought back food and repaired the dock.

The nobles of the Iron Islands regarded Botley as a vassal who relied on sea routes for survival. It does not have the reputation of the entire island like Pike, but it can participate in every archipelago dispute through ships, harbors and kinship relationships; the choice of a small family sometimes determines whether the king can assemble a fleet.

The people of Portley were familiar with salt winds, fishing nets and tides. The sailor evaluates whether the lord understands the sea, and the farmer evaluates whether he remembers that the island also needs food. If the price of iron is nothing more than taking away other people’s things, your own children will eventually starve.
Entry Botley Entry Botley The family crest is just a facade, the real weight of the family is whether they can protect their fiefdom, honor their engagements, and rally people in times of crisis.
Entry Botley Entry Botley Family reputation ultimately comes down to specific people and specific orders.

Entry Botley Entry Botley The ancestors of a family can be praised, or they can become a shackles for future generations; the older the bloodline, the more old debts the successors are required to bear.
Entry Botley Entry Botley They may not remember the complete family tree, but they remember which family opened a granary in the winter and which family drove the refugees back into the snow.
